title: Transportation & Logistics
summary: Asset-heavy carriers, asset-light 3PLs, and freight brokerages where network density, technology, and labor management drive margins.
businessModel: Moving goods from origin to destination via trucking, rail, or air, or acting as an intermediary (broker/3PL) to arrange transportation.
revenueModel: Transactional revenue per load, contract-based dedicated fleet revenue, or brokerage margins (spread between customer price and carrier cost).
costStructure: For asset-heavy: fuel, driver compensation, maintenance, and equipment depreciation. For asset-light: purchased transportation (carrier pay) and personnel.
whyPeLikesIt: PE is attracted to the immense fragmentation, the essential/non-discretionary nature of freight, and the vast opportunity to deploy technology to improve routing, pricing, and back-office efficiency.
investmentThesis: Consolidate regional carriers or brokerages to build network density, implement advanced Transportation Management Systems (TMS) to optimize routing and pricing, and shift revenue mix toward sticky, contractual relationships.
diligenceQuestions: What is the mix of spot market versus contractual freight?
How severe is driver turnover and what is the cost per hire?
Is the technology stack capable of real-time visibility and dynamic pricing?
operationalIssues: High empty miles (deadhead) eroding asset profitability.
Severe driver shortage and high turnover rates.
Manual pricing and load-matching processes in brokerages.
aiOpportunities: Predictive routing and load matching to eliminate empty miles.
Dynamic pricing models for spot freight.
Predictive maintenance for fleet assets to prevent breakdowns.
risks: Regulatory changes (e.g., hours of service, emissions).
Labor unionization or driver misclassification risks.
hundredDayPlan: Implement daily tracking of key operational metrics (Empty miles, OR, Margin per load).
Optimize fuel purchasing agreements and maintenance vendor contracts.
exitReadiness: Demonstrated resilience through freight market cycles.
High percentage of contractual, recurring revenue.
State-of-the-art TMS and visibility tech stack.

articleSections.title: Network Density and Route Optimization
body: In asset-heavy transportation and logistics, profitability is universally governed by the 'Operating Ratio' (Operating Expenses divided by Net Sales). The most effective, non-inflationary way to lower this ratio and expand margins is by aggressively increasing 'Network Density.' Every time a commercial truck drives without freight in the trailer—a scenario known in the industry as 'Empty Miles' or 'Deadhead'—it burns expensive fuel and accrues labor costs without generating a single dollar of revenue. Private Equity value creation focuses intensely on acquiring overlapping regional carriers to create denser, contiguous freight networks.

We systematically implement advanced routing algorithms and enterprise-grade Transportation Management Systems (TMS), such as McLeod or TMW, to optimize asset utilization. By analyzing vast amounts of historical lane data and predicting future volume trends, dispatchers can string together continuous, revenue-generating routes, often referred to as 'triangulation.' This optimization can reliably reduce empty miles from an industry-average of 15-20% down to under 10%. Because fixed costs remain static, this operational discipline drops directly to the bottom line as pure profit.

Furthermore, dense networks allow carriers to pivot from volatile, low-margin 'spot market' freight to highly desirable 'dedicated' or contractual freight. When a carrier can guarantee capacity in specific lanes due to network density, shippers are willing to sign multi-year agreements. For a $200M carrier, improving asset utilization by just 5% can yield $10M+ in incremental EBITDA, expanding margins significantly without requiring the capital expenditure of adding a single new truck to the fleet.
articleSections.callout: In logistics, density is destiny. Empty miles are the silent killer of the Operating Ratio, and eliminating them is pure profit flow-through.

articleSections.title: Tech-Enablement in Freight Brokerage
body: Asset-light freight brokerages (3PLs) operate entirely on the margin spread between what a shipper pays to move a load and what the underlying carrier charges to haul it. Historically, this industry relied on 'boiler rooms' of brokers making manual phone calls and sending mass emails to match available loads with truck capacity. The modern Private Equity playbook transforms these labor-intensive businesses through severe tech-enablement, moving from an analog brokerage to a 'Digital Freight Matching' platform.

We deploy sophisticated, API-driven platforms that instantly connect shipper demand with carrier capacity, eliminating the need for manual negotiation on routine lanes. By integrating automated pricing algorithms that scrape real-time spot market data, we ensure that brokers are quoting rates that are highly competitive yet structurally profitable. This 'Digital Brokerage' approach radically increases the number of loads handled per broker per day—often driving a 30-50% increase in productivity—while simultaneously reducing the error rate inherent in manual data entry.

The financial impact of this tech-enablement is profound operating leverage. As the platform scales revenue, it does not need to linearly scale its headcount, allowing gross margin improvements to flow unimpeded to EBITDA. We establish daily KPIs tracking 'Loads per Broker' and 'Brokerage Margin %,' expecting the Operating Partner to utilize this real-time visibility to correct underperforming teams instantly. A tech-enabled 3PL is ultimately viewed as a software-like asset at exit, commanding a massive multiple premium over traditional, manual brokerages.

articleSections.title: Driver Retention as a Core Profit Center
body: The transportation industry suffers from a chronic, systemic shortage of qualified commercial drivers, with annualized turnover rates frequently exceeding 90% in the over-the-road truckload sector. Recruiting, onboarding, and training a single new driver costs between $5,000 and $8,000, and while a truck sits idle in the yard waiting for a driver, the company bleeds fixed costs. We fundamentally reframe driver retention from a soft HR issue into a hard, quantifiable operational profit center.

Value creation in human capital involves implementing structured career pathways, aggressively upgrading to modern, comfortable equipment, and ensuring predictable home time through smarter, data-driven dispatching. We also deploy in-cab telematics to build 'Driver Performance Scorecards'—tracking metrics like hard braking, idling time, and fuel efficiency—which are directly linked to incentive pay. This shifts the culture from adversarial to collaborative, rewarding drivers who treat the equipment as if they owned it.

By applying these professionalized retention strategies, we target a reduction in turnover by at least 20-30%. For a mid-sized carrier employing 1,000 drivers, reducing turnover from 90% to 60% saves nearly $2M annually in direct recruiting costs, while unlocking millions more in hidden EBITDA through increased asset utilization and reduced accident frequency. A carrier with a stable, tenured driver base is a highly resilient asset, insulated from the labor shocks that frequently devastate less disciplined competitors.

articleSections.title: Procurement Leverage and Working Capital Management
body: Transportation is an inherently capital-intensive and asset-heavy industry, making procurement and working capital management vital levers for EBITDA expansion. During the first 100 days, we aggregate purchasing spend across all acquired platforms to negotiate dominant national accounts for diesel fuel, tires, replacement parts, and commercial insurance. Implementing rigorous fuel hedging strategies and forcing driver compliance with in-network fueling stations can reliably shave pennies off every mile, translating to massive savings at scale.

On the working capital side, 3PLs and carriers frequently suffer from crippling Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) as massive corporate shippers stretch payment terms to 60 or 90 days, while owner-operator carriers demand rapid pay (often within 48 hours). We professionalize the invoicing and collections process, implementing automated auditing and electronic billing to eliminate the manual errors that shippers use as excuses to delay payment. We target a reduction in DSO to under 35 days across the portfolio.

Optimizing this cash conversion cycle frees up the critical liquidity necessary to fund further strategic acquisitions or execute dividend recapitalizations without drawing down expensive revolving credit facilities. A highly disciplined finance function that flawlessly manages the spread between accounts receivable and accounts payable is essential for surviving the inevitable cyclical downturns in the freight market, ensuring the platform remains cash-generative regardless of macroeconomic conditions.
